Any line or choice may carry if_flag, if_not_flag, if_item, if_not_item or if_chapter. Wording is written for the game; the few short book lines kept are listed in quotes.json.

lines.n: I lay in bed, watching the moonlight shift across the floor. The house had been quiet for hours now, but his rage was still in it, in the wood and the stone and the glass.

I didn't want to think about anything Rhysand had said. Not the sickness, nor Under the Mountain, wherever that was, nor why anyone would haul me there. Not Amarantha. The shadow that hung over all of them had a name now: a female dangerous enough to give orders to High Lords. To keep Rhysand on a chain, and bring Tamlin to his knees.
The door creaked, and I jerked upright. Moonlight on gold. My heart didn't settle as he shut the door and crossed to the bed, his steps slow and heavy.
He sat on the edge of the mattress, and for a long moment said nothing at all.
A lie. If I let myself, I could still feel those claws of power raking across my mind.
He pulled one of my hands free of the sheets and held it, and hung his head.
He shook his head and cleared his throat.
Something inside me splintered.

lines.t: I've taken on your debt. If anyone comes asking about the broken law, I'll answer for Andras's death myself.
You said there was no other way out. The Suriel said...
Anyone who objects can come and say so to my face.

lines.n: And end up in ribbons.
He pressed my hand to his cheek, so warm, and turned his face to kiss my palm.

lines.t: You did nothing wrong. You were perfect.
Then why do I have to go?

Because there are people who would hurt you for what you are to me. I thought I could shield you from it. After today, I know I can't. So you have to go home, far away from here. You'll be safe there.
You can't. Because I can't. I can't even shield myself from them, or from whatever's coming for Prythian. Even if we held off the sickness, they'd come after you. She would find some way to end you.

lines.n: He bristled at the name, but nodded.

lines.t: Once you're home, tell nobody the truth about where you've been. Leave the glamour be. Don't speak of me, or of this place. She'll have eyes looking for you.
I want to stay with you. Treaty or no Treaty. Sickness or no sickness.

This isn't up for discussion! Rhys was the first of them. Do you want to still be under this roof when the Attor comes back? Do you want to meet the thing it serves? Creatures like the Bogge, and worse than the Bogge.
So that's it? I'm going because I'd be no use to you in a fight?
You're going because the thought of them getting hold of you turns my stomach!

lines.n: Then quiet, except for his rough breathing. He dropped down on the edge of the bed and ground his palms into his eyes, and all my anger drained away.

lines.t: How long? A week? A month?

lines.n: He shook his head, slowly.
Even if the sickness came here, even if it tore me apart, I would come back.

lines.t: I expect you'll be relieved. Who'd want to keep a girl who's all prickles?

lines.n: He leaned in and kissed me, lightly.
I could tell he was lying. I wrapped my arms round his neck and kissed him all the same.

choices.t: Hold him, and only hold him.

lines.n: Rhysand's touch still clawed at the edges of my mind. I pushed it away, and pushed him down onto the bed, as if holding him there could stop the night from ending.

do.text: The rest of that night belonged to the two of them.

lines.n: Afterward we lay tangled in the moonlight, and I breathed him in. Earth, and something crisp. I would never be able to paint the feel of him, however many colors I tried.

lines.t: Sleep now. You've a long way to go in the morning.

lines.n: Please. He had knelt to Rhysand for my sake.
I didn't want anything but this. I lay with my head on his chest, his heart under my ear, and held on as if I could stop the night from ending.

lines.t: Get some rest. It's a long road home.

lines.n: Please. He had knelt to Rhysand for my sake.
He started to ease away toward the edge of the bed.

lines.t: If I stay here, neither of us will sleep.
Stay. I'll behave. I swear it.

lines.n: A lie. An outright lie. His half smile said he knew it, but he lay down and pulled me into his arms and stroked my hair.
I didn't want to sleep. I didn't want to lose a single minute with him. But exhaustion was dragging me under.

I was going. Just as this place had turned into more than a refuge, and he into so much more than the one who'd rescued me, or a friend. Years might pass before I breathed in his roses again, or looked into those gold-flecked eyes. This was home now.
As sleep finally took me, I thought I felt his breath at my ear, and heard him whisper.

lines.t: I love you. Thorns and all.

lines.n: When I woke, his side of the bed was cold. I was sure I'd only dreamed it.
